study: Shechtman et al. 2019, Reasoning Mind RM-CC5 digital core math curriculum (MCIS)
eval_evidence: Report states the 'study was conducted by an independent evaluation team, not Reasoning Mind' (SRI/MCIS, IES/NCEE efficacy grant).
developer_evidence: Implementation coordinators (ICs) 'employed by Reasoning Mind' (the program developer) provided the ~60 hours of teacher PD and ongoing coaching; developer staff delivered the PD (even though the impact evaluation was independent).
cascade_evidence: Reasoning Mind ICs delivered the PD and coaching directly to teachers (each school assigned an IC); no train-the-trainer hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools continued their existing business-as-usual Grade 5 mathematics curriculum/resources.
coaching_evidence: ICs 'conducted classroom observations regularly... and coached teachers in improving instruction... throughout the year'; each school had an assigned IC providing ongoing in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: RM-CC5 is an adaptive, blended digital core curriculum students work through on the computer with software feedback — a substantial student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: 2-year RCT: Year 1 (SY2014-15) was the 'warm-up year' for teacher development; Year 2 (SY2015-16) was the 'measurement year' — outcomes measured after one prior implementation year (experienced teachers).
